p01.about: Turn a blunt message into an email you can send.
try: Your invoice is wrong again. Fix it.
No, I can't make another meeting this week.
We told you this last month.

p02.about: Describe the thing you can't quite remember and get five guesses.
try: that Excel feature that fills a pattern for you
a film about a chess prodigy

p03.about: Learn the essentials of a new topic, fast.
p03.note: Good for getting started. Your data protection team has the final word.

p04.about: Describe what you need and get an Excel formula, explained.
try: counts how many names appear more than once
shows the latest date for each name

p05.about: Hear the strongest objections to your idea before your colleagues raise them.
try: switching our team updates from email to Teams
cutting our monthly report to one page

p06.about: Practise a difficult conversation, with Copilot as your manager. Type DEBRIEF when you're done.

p07.about: Get quizzed on any topic, one question at a time.

p08.about: See how four different readers would take your message.

p09.about: Turn corporate jargon into plain English.

upload.text: Or upload a letter or policy

p10.about: Rewrite any text so a 12-year-old could follow it.

upload.text: Or upload a photo of a letter or form

p11.about: Make a cold notice sound warm without changing a single rule.

p12.about: Get three ways to say no: warm, firm, and not now.
try: extra work on a Friday afternoon

p13.about: Turn blunt notes into feedback a colleague can take.

p14.about: Turn a rambling voice note into a short, clear email.

upload.text: Click the microphone (Start Dictation) and speak

p15.about: Turn technical text into a 100-word summary for the public.

upload.text: Or upload the report or spec

p16.about: Translate a sentence and flag what a translator should check.
try: a sentence of your own (second bracket)
p16.note: Official bilingual material still goes through your translation service.

p17.about: Get ten name ideas, half serious and half playful.
try: a project to cut paper use

p21.about: Imagine a project has failed and list the reasons why.

p22.about: Spot the side effects of a change before you launch it.

p23.about: See what a change gains and what it costs, side by side.
try: a single shared inbox for the team

p24.about: Review a plan from three different points of view.
try: a plan to move the team to hot-desking
a plan to shorten opening hours
a plan to move a service online

p25.about: Read your guidance as the person who has to follow it.
try: a paragraph of your own guidance

p26.about: Get an honest critique of your writing, with no flattery.

upload.text: Or upload your bid or report

p27.about: Find the claims in a proposal to check before you present.
try: a sentence or two from a proposal
the summary of a business case

p28.about: Get three questions that challenge your plan.

p29.about: Get asked the one key question before any answers.
try: our plan to move training online
our plan to merge two newsletters
our plan to change the rota
p29.note: Answer it, then type "next question" to keep going.

p30.about: Get weighted criteria for comparing options or suppliers.

p31.about: Work out why you keep putting a task off, and how to start.

p34.about: Get one idea explained for a child, a colleague and an expert.

p35.about: Get an everyday comparison that makes a technical idea stick.
p35.note: Then ask: "Where does this analogy break down?"

p36.about: Answer five questions and get a draft written from your answers.
try: a case study for our newsletter
a handover note for my cover

p37.about: Turn any task into a step-by-step checklist.

p38.about: Get a first-draft procedure, with steps to check flagged.

p39.about: Get a case study outline with gaps where the figures go.
try: a team moving to a shared inbox
a service extending its opening hours

p41.about: Pull the decisions and actions out of messy meeting notes.
p41.note: Swap real names for roles or initials before you paste.

upload.text: Or upload a photo of your notes or whiteboard

p42.about: Turn rough project notes into a log of risks and issues.

upload.text: Or upload your notes as a Word document or PDF

p43.about: Turn a list of topics into a timed meeting agenda.
try: the items for your next team meeting

p44.about: Find the tasks that stop when one person is off.

p45.about: Find the vague wording in a brief, with clearer rewrites.

p46.about: Get a tighter summary by telling Copilot what to leave out.
p46.note: A summary is a starting point. Check the Act itself before you rely on it.

upload.text: Or upload a strategy or report

p47.about: Sort survey comments into themes, in a fixed layout.
p47.note: Remove names and anything that identifies a person first.

upload.text: Or upload a spreadsheet of comments

p54.about: Get a short briefing with a source and a date on every point.
p54.note: Click the sources. Some will be weak or out of date.

p55.about: Compare a web-search answer with one from Copilot's memory.
try: How long can we keep personal data?
What are the rules on flexible working requests?
p55.note: Click a link in the first answer and check it says what Copilot claims.

p57.about: See what Copilot does when you ask about something it cannot see.
p57.note: In Copilot Chat a good answer admits it has no access. A bad one makes things up.

p58.about: Test whether Copilot can quote the law word for word. It often cannot.
try: the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974
p58.note: Check every quote and section number on legislation.gov.uk.

p59.about: Give Copilot a logic puzzle and see whether it spots the catch.
p59.note: The catch: this rota is impossible. A good answer says so; many draw a neat table that breaks the rules.
